facts.content: Patient presents with an acute severe headache.
The headache began yesterday morning.
The headache is left-sided and throbbing.
The headache is associated with photophobia and is worse in bright light.
Lying down helps relieve the headache.
The patient reports no nausea, vomiting, or eye symptoms with the headache.
facts.source_text: no nausea, vomiting, or eye symptoms

facts.content: The patient reports no fever or upper respiratory infection symptoms associated with the headache.
The patient states this is their first-ever headache.
The patient reports possible stress at work as a trigger.
The headache is not clearly linked to the menstrual cycle.
facts.source_text: not clearly linked to menstrual cycle

facts.content: The patient’s last menstrual period occurred about one week ago.
The patient has no significant past medical or surgical history reported.
The patient has taken paracetamol.
The patient takes daily Microgynon contraception, started approximately six years ago.
The patient is allergic to aspirin, which causes sickness if taken.
The patient’s mother has hypertension.
The patient’s mother has migraines.
The patient reports a family history of migraines.
The patient lives with housemates.
The patient uses alcohol on weekends.
The patient is a non-smoker.
The patient does not use illicit drugs.
The clinician assesses an acute, new-onset left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia with a pattern suggestive of migraine without aura.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute, new-onset left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia; pattern suggestive of migraine without aura

facts.content: No red flags are documented in the headache history.
facts.source_text: no red flags documented in history.

facts.content: The clinician notes an aspirin allergy.
The clinician notes a family history of migraines.
Plan is symptomatic management with NSAID plus paracetamol.
The patient is advised to ensure good hydration.
The patient is advised to rest in a dark and quiet room.
The patient is educated to avoid bright light and monitor symptoms.
facts.source_text: Education: avoid bright light, monitor symptoms

facts.content: The patient is instructed to seek urgent review if the headache worsens or if fever, new neurological symptoms, neck stiffness, or rash develop.
facts.source_text: if headache worsens or if fever, new neuro symptoms, neck stiffness, rash arise, seek urgent review.

facts.content: The clinician plans to consider longer-term migraine management if headaches recur, persist, or are linked to menses and to discuss this at follow-up.
facts.source_text: Consider longer-term migraine management if headaches recur, persist, or are linked to menses; discuss at follow-up.

facts.content: The plan includes checking blood pressure if it has not been checked recently.
facts.source_text: Monitoring: check blood pressure (BP) if not recently checked

facts.content: The plan includes obtaining home blood pressure monitoring.
The patient is advised to obtain a thermometer to track temperature.
facts.source_text: obtain a thermometer to track temperature.

facts.content: The patient is advised to return as needed or sooner if red flags or persistent symptoms occur.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: return PRN or sooner if red flags or persistent symptoms

facts.content: The clinician plans to reassess if the headache is not settling within 1–2 days or if new symptoms develop.
facts.source_text: clinician to reassess if not settling within 1–2 days or if new symptoms develop.
